name: Social media post (LinkedIn, 1:1 and 4:5)
note: Rules set by the brand team on 2026-10-23 (Figma page Social media). Posts are designed at 540 px wide and exported at 2x (1080 px), so every size and space is a design-system style or token. The reference posts in Figma show layout and feel only; they need not match the design system.

typography.note: Sizes are at the 540 px design size; double them at 1080.

headline.use: the main message of the post

cover_headline.use: the headline on a cover slide

subheadline.use: the line beside a big number

metric.use: big numbers and results; Bold only when the user asks, never larger

metric_in_grid.use: big numbers in a stat grid

roles.label: Role/Label: tags, chart labels and the series label
roles.caption: Role/Caption: source or legal line

dark.note: Mapped from the designed slides' #132335 to the nearest token.

content.rule: No fixed theme or order: pick each slide's theme from the social templates and its content (brand-blue step posts with a big stat and a visual, dark stat tiles, light quote slides), unless the user asks for one. Mix themes across a carousel so it never reads as one colour.

spacing.note: Spacing roles at the 540 px design size; double them at 1080. The grid keeps its 12 px gutter (spacing/12).

gap/inline.use: between adjacent items: an icon and its label, chips

gap/stack.use: between stacked elements inside a card or block

padding/container.use: inside every card, box and panel

spacing.card: UI cards and boxes use the container default: container/primary (container/secondary on light when the card sits on white), 1px border/container, radius/3xl (12px), padding/container. On dark slides the same container tokens in the dark colour mode; on brand slides container/inverse with text/inverse (the templates' dark caption boxes) or container/primary. Size each card to its content.

content_forms.rule: Before designing a slide, name the shape of its content and draw it in the matching form, built from design-system parts and the blocks (Stat tile, Process flow, Comparison table, Feature grid, Quote card). The social templates show each form. A row of text cards or a bare list is never the form for steps, results or a problem.
content_forms.references: get_brand_guidelines(section: "data-viz"): reference layouts for numbers, steps, stages, cycles and systems (stat layouts, charts, funnel, flywheel, staircase, plant drawings), the same in every format. References, not fixed layouts: build designs like them, adapted to the content.

forms.numbers: A result or KPI: one big number (Display/XL Regular) with its label, and a visual of the change (before and after bars, a line settling into a band, a gauge); several results: stat tiles in a 2x2 or 3-up grid, one highlighted.
forms.sequence: Steps or a change in how work is done: an icon flow (icons converging into one pill, or numbered nodes with connectors) with short text under each.
forms.problem_solution: A problem and its answer, or before and after: a split contrast, the problem side in the Negative intent and the answer in brand or Positive.
forms.comparison: Before and after, or options: labelled bars or a compact comparison table.
forms.like_items: Parallel items (data sources, capabilities, pain points): cards or tiles with a Lucide icon per item, sized to their content, or an icon grid.
forms.quote: A customer or leader quote: a quote card with the highlighted phrase, name and role, and the headshot from the asset library where it exists.
forms.message: One statement or call to action (cover, closing): the headline as the hero, with a design element where the background allows it.

product_visuals.rule: A post that shows a product screen (an I/O Sense dashboard, the Bruce AI product visual, an operator view) uses the user's screenshot. There is no product screenshot library, so without one place a placeholder; never draw a fake product UI.
product_visuals.placeholder: A frame at the size and position the design needs: container/secondary, 1px dashed border/strong, radius/3xl, with the label DASHBOARD_MOCKUP_<NAME> centred in Body/LG text/secondary. List every placeholder in the delivery note.

photos: Photos (the case-study cover, quote backgrounds) come only from the user, in the imagery styles (section "imagery"). There is no photography library; never use stock, generated or sampled photos. Ask when a layout needs one.

logo.position: top-right by default; top-left when the slide design needs it
logo.place: An from the asset's url (get_brand_guidelines(section: "assets", asset_category: "logos")) with alt "Faclon Labs"; never a placeholder box, a text label or a redrawn logo.

bruce_ai.note: Figma paint style (blue to pink). Used only on Bruce AI content, for example the headline or a highlight.

guardrails.note: Guidance for whoever designs in this format. user_decides = what is made (the user's call); fixed = do not change; must_not = hard limits; avoid = strong advice; design_direction = how to use the system; claude_decides = how it looks, where the designer has freedom. Every design item cites its basis in the design system.
user_decides: What is being made, for whom and why: the post, its purpose and audience.
The content and facts. The designer uses exactly what the user supplies or approves: never invents, adds, rewrites, shortens or cuts it, and asks before suggesting a change.
The scope: a single post or a carousel, and how many slides. Nothing is added that was not asked for; when it is unclear, ask.
Square or portrait (the designer can suggest), and the call to action and link, if any.
The cover image: the user generates it and shares it.
A slide's theme, when they want a particular one; otherwise the designer picks it from the templates and the content.

fixed.text: Square 1:1 (540 × 540 px) or portrait 4:5 (540 × 675 px), designed at 540 px wide and exported at 2x (1080 × 1080 or 1080 × 1350). A set of posts can mix both.
24 px safe area on all sides (spacing/24); content 492 px wide. Text, the logo and content stay inside it; only images may bleed to the edge.
12 columns inside the safe area: 30 px columns with 12 px gutters (spacing/12).
Text uses the style set for its element (headline Heading/H1 Bold, body Body/LG, big numbers Display/XL Regular), between 10px and 72px.
The full Faclon Labs logo on every post and slide, top-right by default (top-left when the design needs it), about 132 px wide: blue on light, white on dark and brand.
Three themes: light (background/primary), dark (background/inverse) and brand (background/brand), each with its fixed text and logo colours.
Delivered as HTML. The user converts it to PNG, JPG or PDF if they need to.

claude_decides: Layout and composition within the grid: what goes where and what leads.
Visual hierarchy: what is large, what is quiet, and how the eye moves.
Which components to use and how to combine them, and new card designs on Card base when the named cards don't fit.
How to show each idea: a stat, a process, a comparison, a story.
Whether a slide needs the logo top-left instead of the default top-right.
How a carousel story is split across slides (as a suggestion when it changes the user's order).

icons.note: Sizes in px at the design size. In a UI card the icon square follows the card: pick the step for the card's width, so a bigger card gets a bigger icon and square (CSS container queries on the card). The square is the icon plus 8px (gap/inline) on every side, a solid fill with no border; square only. Figma: the Icon square component (Size = icon size).
